title: Arcade Snack Rush: Crew Drill
premise: Run a neon-styled snack stand inside a three-wing arcade venue by taking orders, cooking food combos, serving tables, managing trays and supplies, and gradually automating the workflow with recruitable staff.
interaction_model: Real-time top-down touch game with a virtual joystick for movement and a single context-sensitive action button for taking orders, cooking, washing, serving, collecting money, training crew, and unlocking rooms.
objective: Earn money and grow throughput by serving customers correctly and quickly, then spend profits on supplies, extra tables, staff recruitment, staff training, and unlocking new wings.
progression: Begin in the central room with a small setup, manually perform the full service loop, recruit specialist staff to automate bottlenecks, train them for speed, add tables, and unlock side wings to expand capacity.
mood: Energetic, colorful, hectic, and lightly playful rather than punishing
likely_audience: players who enjoy simple management loops with automation upgrades

high_confidence: The game is a real-time cooking/service management sim with direct avatar control.
Staff roles automate order taking, cooking, washing, and money collection.
Expansion and resource management are central to progression.
medium_confidence: The arcade framing appears to be thematic packaging around a restaurant-service loop rather than a separate minigame layer.
The intended long-term pacing likely emphasizes automation and room expansion, though the code does not define a final win state.
low_confidence: Any narrative framing beyond the title and visual theme is minimal.
There is no explicit endgame or campaign structure in the code.

recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first top-down arcade-styled restaurant management game called "Arcade Snack Rush: Crew Drill" where the player controls a snack-stand runner inside a neon three-wing venue using a virtual joystick and a single context-sensitive action button. Start in the center wing with a grill, sink, trash can, counter, and a couple of tables, while the left and right wings are locked and can later be purchased. Customers spawn over time, queue at the counter with visible food requests, get assigned to tables when orders are taken, wait with patience bars, eat when served the correct meal, and then leave money on tables to collect. Let the player manually run the whole loop: take orders at the counter, open a cooking menu to prepare burgers, pizza, salad, or sushi, spend supplies and clean trays when cooking, pick up finished food, deliver it to the matching table, wash trays at the sink to refill dish capacity, and discard unwanted held food in the trash. Add light management systems: money, ingredient stock, tray count, payroll every minute, purchasable supply packs, extra tables, and room unlocks. Include recruitable staff such as cashier, chef, waiter, and washer who automate order-taking, cooking, cash pickup, and dish washing, plus an in-world training mechanic where the player stands near a staff member, pays cash, and holds through a timed drill to level them up and improve speed. Present everything with a clean canvas playfield plus stylish HUD overlays, upgrade and cooking modals, floating feedback text, bright arcade UI fonts, celebratory and warning visual feedback, and a lively but readable mobile layout. The overall feel should be a fast, casual, colorful service-management loop that shifts from manual multitasking into semi-automated tycoon-like flow as the crew and venue expand.
